rubrics_metrics.name: Design and material criteria for perpetual sepulchral lamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and design considerations discussed for making 'perpetual' sepulchral lamps: choice of wick and fuel, and experimental approaches to reproduce ancient lamp behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points recorded in text: prefer linum asbestinum (salamander's wool) as wick if perpetual oil is available; metalline wire (annealed iron, silver, gold) was tested and judged unlikely to work as a wick; consider local bitumen/naphta (e.g., Pitchford, Shropshire) as a source of almost inexhaustible oil, separable before it joins water; note that some ancient lamps burned best in close damp vaults and were extinguished by admission of air — this suggests a fuel/flame type that burns with little air; miners' blue flame in coal fissures (burns best with least air) is proposed as suitable; an alternative experimental construction: include liquid phosphorus in a stopped phial inside an exhausted recipient so that admission of air would make it shine (mimicking urns that light when opened). Examples and caveats (from author): some ancient lamps did burn well in open air; bitumen burns better with moisture; some lamps may only appear when air admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol for anatomical observation of lacteals and chyle
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental procedures and interpretive criteria used to observe lacteals and the colour/contents of chyle in dogs (three experiments described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods and procedural details: (Exper. I) keep dog fasting (48–72 hours), open and cut several lacteals to observe transparent liquor; (Exper. II) let fasting dog lap a quart of common water, open after 1 hour and observe pellucid lacteals; (Exper. III) give fasting dog fat meat then water and open after times given, tie ductus thoracicus before examination to inspect lacteals, note many white, some diluted white, many pellucid vessels and colour changes along intestine. Interpretive criteria: chyle may be white, pellucid, or intermediate; lacteals may convey other humours besides chyle; timing after feeding, type of aliment (water, broth, milk, fat meat) and location along intestines affect observed colour; consider possible sources (pancreas, liver, intestinal glands) and be cautious about excluding water entry into lacteals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design for freezing saline and mineral solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up comparative freezing trials in identical containers to observe differences between solutions (natron water, nitrum murarium solution, sea water, natural brine/sulphur well brine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lister's protocol: expose glass bottles containing different solutions to the open air on the ground during freezing nights and inspect over successive mornings. Record timing and extent of ice/icicle formation, physical form of ice (flakes, oblong squares), brittleness, transparency, taste (saltiness), behaviour when heated (melting into water vs drying to salt/powder), and longevity of salt icicles vs ordinary ice when brought indoors. Noted conclusions to be verified: sea water can form 'salt ice' with distinct properties, natural brine differs from sea water in salts yielded, and persistence of salt ice may contribute to floating ice masses' longevity. Also an interpretive conjecture about Egyptian nitre origin (comparison with sal ammoniac) is offered but flagged as erroneous in a later note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting clinical/medical observations and interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: How to record clinical cases, observed pathological signs, treatments administered, and outcomes in case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in text: report symptoms and direct observations (e.g., worms in patient's urine; eye tumours described as 'black, fleshy, and full of bluish bladders'); list therapeutic steps and dosages (purges with pil. agaric and rhubarb; oxymel helleboratum in tansy water; 4-an ounce dose given) and surgical interventions (cutting out ulcered flesh, tying, bleeding) with healing time and outcome (wore black patch). For disease interpretation also include differential reasoning (diagnosing cancer vs hydropic eye) and rationale for chosen remedies (drying medicines, making an issue in nucha).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and describing insect observations (morphology & behaviour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for reporting insect observations: habitat/occurrence notes, behaviour (e.g., flight and attraction to lights), seasonality, and detailed morphological description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (cicindela volans): record rarity and specific localities, behaviour (flies about the candle on hot evenings), seasonal dependence (only at certain seasons/hot weather), and morphological details (wing sheaths dusky coloured, head covered like an inverted flat shield, black head with two tubercles/eyes, tail segmented with pellucid drops that shine; note colour range of luminescence and effects of compressing tail). Compare with known species and cite classical descriptions (Aldrovandus) or Linnaean identifications where relevant.
